doc.title: Billy Bauer interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, March 22, 1998

title: Chubby Jackson and Sonny Berman roughhousing
summary: Chubby knocked down Sonny Berman and Bauer in horseplay; Bauer says Chubby played with the same unsophisticated drive.

story.theme_name: Band pranks, jokes and gigs gone wrong
story.community_name: Pranks, practical jokes and band humor

blocks.x: We were talking before the cameras were rolling about one thing with Chubby Jackson. Something about he actually took you down one day, and who was the other fellow you were talking about?

Yeah. Well we used to kid around. We had a lot of different things. And Chubby was always, well I guess he was an athlete. You know he was a dancer, I know he always used to — I don’t know if he could really dance — but he was always strong like, and he was big. At that time he was big. Is he big now?

Well he was, see? And we was kidding around or something and Chubby says, “Ahh shut up, I’ll give it to ya.” So I don’t know, Sonny says, “Yeah whadda ya mean?” And boom, he knocked him down. He didn’t hit him, but he knocked him down and he pinned him down. And then he grabbed me—
He put you down too, huh? He is a spark plug, I’ll give him that.
Oh yeah. And he played that way too. Like he wasn’t sophisticated with what pitches you’re playing or things like that.
